Speaker: Adam
What was said: Thanks for talking to me. Can you tell me what it is like, living with Moss?

Speaker: Ellis
What was said: Moss is a greyhound, an old racer, and he is eleven now. I got him the winter after I retired. Honestly I thought he would be company for the house, something breathing in the next room. I did not expect him to be company for me.
Margin: Company for the house first, then for her. Something breathing in the next room.

Speaker: Ellis
What was said: He watches me. Not in a needy way. He just keeps an eye on where I am, and if I go upstairs he comes and lies on the landing. I had not been kept an eye on for a long time.
Margin: Kept an eye on: watched over, not watched.

Speaker: Adam
What was said: Can you tell me about a day with him?

Speaker: Ellis
What was said: Slow. He is old and so am I, so we suit each other. A short walk at eight, a long sleep, a short walk at four. In between I do my crossword and he sighs at me. People think greyhounds need a lot of running. They need a sofa.
Margin: Slow days that suit them both. The sigh as a kind of talk.

Speaker: Adam
What was said: And when he sighs at you?

Speaker: Ellis
What was said: It feels like he is telling me something, and I answer him. Out loud. My son caught me at it once and laughed, and I was a bit embarrassed, but I did not stop.
Margin: Answering him out loud, and not stopping when caught.

Speaker: Adam
What was said: What would the house be like without him?

Speaker: Ellis
What was said: I try not to think about it. He is eleven, and I know what eleven means for a big dog. When he is slow getting up in the morning I stand and wait, and I do not breathe until he is on his feet.
Margin: Not breathing until he is up. His age known and not said.
